policy_title: End Immigration Detention of Children and Limit Adult Detention
stated: End the detention of children for immigration purposes, and reduce detention for adults to an absolute last resort, with a 28-day time limit.

source.quote: End the detention of children for immigration purposes, and reduce detention for adults to an absolute last resort, with a 28-day time limit.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly curtails deprivation of liberty (a core civil right) for children and adults in immigration proceedings, adds a statutory due-process protection (28-day cap), and specifically protects a vulnerable group from open-ended detention — squarely within O9's strict scope of civil liberties, due process, and equal treatment.

A 28-day hard limit means adults awaiting removal who cannot be removed within that window must be released into the community; the concrete mechanism is that some individuals (including those with criminal histories facing deportation) would be at large longer than under current indefinite detention, which is a genuinely contested but non-negligible effect on the crime-rates and national-security-posture indicators.

Ending child detention and capping adult detention at 28 days directly withdraws state coercive power (physical deprivation of liberty without criminal conviction), improving personal liberty for detainees — the clearest possible bearing on O10.

membership_note: O10 (liberty/coercion) and O9 (due process/rule of law) are both real and distinct: the former scores the physical-freedom effect, the latter the legal-protection framework. O5 (national security) has a diffuse but weak mechanism — reducing immigration detention does not plausibly move crime rates or security posture at a non-negligible level for the general detainee population, so excluded.
